title: Two BART technology approvals cited agreements that did not cover the purchases

beats.text: How can two board approvals point to agreements that do not cover the purchases?

visual.sub: Two different purchasing requests used the same exemption

beats.text: In August 2020, BART approved an Oracle cloud subscription.
The second approval included telecommunications hardware and software.

visual.kicker: Two different purchasing requests used the same exemption

beats.text: For Oracle, California had never authorized that cloud agreement.

visual.kicker: The same claim hid two different documentation failures

beats.text: For SHI, the available agreement excluded hardware.
Inspectors found legitimate business needs. They measured no overpayment.
All four recommendations were marked implemented in the fiscal 2022 report.

visual.label: A retest reversed a completed training recommendation

beats.text: A later retest found that recurring training had never been assigned.

visual.kicker: A retest reversed a completed training recommendation

beats.text: Training was still in progress on November 23.
A separate 2026 Cisco vote showed what a verifiable approval looks like.

visual.kicker: A later vote shows how the prerequisite could be checked

beats.text: The report named both agreements. The signed state amendment covered the vote date.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
